headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; no documented isolation between firecrawl and ms-swift.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl can ingest web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API scraping surfaces, while ms-swift reads stdin/stdout and files. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from firecrawl be treated as instructions by ms-swift. No direct isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is copied into ms-swift prompts or files without sanitization
IF both agents share a writable workspace or message queue
mitigations: Use a separate directory for firecrawl outputs and ms-swift inputs
Strip instructions from scraped text before passing it onward
Add a manual review step for any web-derived prompt content
Disable automatic ingestion of raw scrape results
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: firecrawl handles API keys and broad web content, and ms-swift reads/writes datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files. If they share a workspace, either agent could expose sensitive material through the other’s outputs or uploads. The profiles do not document isolation, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF firecrawl stores scraped secrets or API keys in files readable by ms-swift
IF ms-swift logs or uploads files from a shared directory
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders
Rotate any API keys used by firecrawl
Restrict ms-swift to a dedicated workspace
Review logs for accidental secret capture
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while ms-swift can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write files. Even though ms-swift does not modify git state, overlapping writes and concurrent file access can still corrupt shared artifacts if they operate in the same directory. Lack of stated locking escalates uncertainty.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact store
IF ms-swift installs packages while firecrawl is running in the same environment
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Run package installs in a disposable environment
Pause one agent during critical file writes
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data, and ms-swift can consume files and run commands. If ms-swift treats firecrawl output as authoritative, bad or manipulated content can cascade into downstream actions or training artifacts. Because no verification step is documented, the default pathway is dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF ms-swift uses firecrawl output as training data, configs, or shell input without validation
IF firecrawl-sourced text is promoted into downstream automation
mitigations: Require human review before acting on scraped content
Validate schemas before importing outputs
Quarantine firecrawl outputs as untrusted
Log source URLs alongside derived artifacts
requires-engineering: add content verification and allowlists

E_compliance.rationale: firecrawl touches API keys and web content, while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data. If regulated or personal data is scraped and then stored or processed by ms-swift, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No certifications or DPA/residency guarantees are documented for either profile, so medium is the prudent level.
conditions: IF scraped content includes personal data, credentials, or regulated records
IF ms-swift retains datasets or logs longer than firecrawl’s source retention
mitigations: Classify scraped data before storage
Delete unnecessary logs and checkpoints promptly
Keep regulated data out of training inputs
Confirm residency and retention settings
requires-engineering: document a shared data-handling policy
